items.prompt: I like mangoes ___ I like bananas.

options.why: Because gives a reason. Liking bananas is not a reason for liking mangoes.
If means only when something happens.
But shows a difference. Here both ideas are the same kind.

hints: Both ideas are about fruit you like.
Which word adds one idea to another?
Read the sentence with each word. Which one sounds natural?
items.explanation: And joins two ideas that go together: I like mangoes and I like bananas.

items.prompt: It was raining, ___ we took an umbrella.

options.why: But shows a surprise. Taking an umbrella in the rain is not a surprise.
Or gives a choice.
If means only when something happens. It really was raining.

hints: What happened because it was raining?
Look for a word that shows a result.
Read it aloud with each word in the gap.
items.explanation: So shows what happened as a result. It was raining, so we took an umbrella.

items.prompt: I wanted to play outside, ___ it was too hot.

options.why: Because gives a reason. Wanting to play is not caused by the heat.
So shows a result. Wanting to play did not make it hot.
Or gives a choice.

hints: Did the child get to play outside?
Look for a word that shows a problem or a difference.
Try each word and read the whole sentence aloud.
items.explanation: But shows a difference between two ideas. I wanted to play, but the heat stopped me.

options.why: So shows a result.
Because gives a reason.
But shows a difference.

hints: This is a question about choosing.
Which word gives a choice between two things?
Imagine someone at a food stall asking you. What would they say?
items.explanation: Or gives a choice. You can have rice or noodles.

items.prompt:
Write so or because in the gap.
Joko wore his coat ___ it was cold.
hints: Why did Joko wear his coat?
One word gives a reason. The other gives a result.
Read the sentence with so. Does it make sense?
items.explanation: Because gives the reason. Joko wore his coat because it was cold.

items.prompt: Match the beginnings to the best endings.
pairs: We can go to the park if
hints: Read the joining word at the end of each beginning.
If shows what must happen first. Because gives a reason. So gives a result.
Start with Ana was tired because. Which ending is a reason for being tired?
items.explanation: Each joining word needs the right kind of ending. Because needs a reason, so needs a result, and if needs something that must happen first.

items.prompt: Bima practised every day ___ he wanted to win the race.

options.why: So shows a result. Wanting to win is the reason, not the result.
Or gives a choice.
If means only when something happens.

hints: Why did Bima practise every day?
You need a word that gives a reason.
Read the sentence with each word and listen to the meaning.
items.explanation: Because gives the reason. Bima practised because he wanted to win.

items.prompt:
Join the two sentences with when.
I get home. I feed my cat.

answers: When I get home, I feed my cat
When I get home I feed my cat
I feed my cat when I get home

hints: When can go at the start or in the middle.
Put when in front of I get home.
If you start with When, put a comma before the second part.
items.explanation: You can write When I get home, I feed my cat. You can also write I feed my cat when I get home.

items.prompt: Choose 2 sentences that use so correctly.

options.text: I was hungry, so I ate a banana.
I ate a banana, so I was hungry.
options.why: Eating a banana does not make you hungry.

options.text: It was dark, so we turned on the light.
We turned on the light, so it was dark.
options.why: Turning on a light does not make a room dark.

hints: So shows a result: what happens next because of the first part.
Check that the first part could really cause the second part.
Take the first sentence. Does being hungry make you eat?
items.explanation: So shows a result. Being hungry makes you eat, and a dark room makes you turn on the light.

options.text: If the seeds grew, because you water them.
options.why: This mixes if and because, and it does not make sense.

options.text: You water the seeds if, they will grow.
options.why: The comma is in the wrong place, and the order is muddled.

options.text: If you water the seeds, they will grow.
If you water the seeds but they will grow.
options.why: But does not fit after an if part.

hints: If tells us what must happen first.
An if sentence has two parts: the if part and what will happen.
Find the sentence with an if part, then a comma, then what will happen.
items.explanation: If you water the seeds tells us what must happen first. They will grow tells us the result.

items.prompt: Lena felt nervous ___ she sang well in the show.

options.why: Singing well is not a reason to feel nervous.
Feeling nervous did not make her sing well.
Or gives a choice.

hints: Is there something surprising in this sentence?
Feeling nervous and singing well do not usually go together.
Which word shows a difference or a surprise?
items.explanation: But shows a surprise. Lena was nervous, but she still sang well.

items.prompt:
Which word shows that the rain stopped first?
We played outside ___ the rain stopped.

options.why: Before means we played first, and then the rain stopped.
Until means we played up to the time the rain stopped.
Or gives a choice. It does not tell us when.

hints: Think about which thing happened first.
Three of these words are about time.
Try each word. Picture what happens first in each sentence.
items.explanation: After means the rain stopped first, and then we played outside.

items.prompt: Put the words in order to make a sentence.
hints: The sentence has two parts joined by and then.
There is a comma after the first part.
Lunch comes before football.
items.explanation: I ate my lunch, and then I played football. And then shows the order of events.
items.answer: I ate my lunch, and then I played football.

items.prompt: I will take an umbrella ___ it might rain.
hints: The second part gives a reason.
Which joining word explains why?
It is the word you use to answer a why question.
items.explanation: Because gives the reason for taking an umbrella.
